q: Who does the statue in the middle of Place des Palmistes depict?
x: Félix Éboué, born in Cayenne, governor and a leading figure of Free France. The monument dates from 1957.

q: Where does the name of Fort Cépérou come from?
x: Cépérou was a Kali'na chief who ceded the hill to the French around 1643.

q: Which soup is the institution of Cayenne market?
x: Under the market hall, phở counters run by Hmong families serve it from breakfast time.

q: In which year was Cayenne's market hall inaugurated?
x: Decided in 1907, the hall was inaugurated in 1910.

q: Which convict painted the penal colony scenes shown at the Franconie museum?
x: Francis Lagrange painted penal colony life. Pierre Huguet is the painter credited with Iracoubo church.

q: Who founded the Loyola estate in 1668?
x: The Jesuits made it a large estate of over 1,000 hectares, with about 500 enslaved people at its peak.

q: Why is the sea brown at Montjoly?
x: The current carries sediment from the Amazon along the coast.

q: Why don't people swim in the Rorota lakes?
x: The trail runs along the Rorota, Lalouette and Rémire lakes, which supply the area with drinking water.

q: How high is the summit of Mont Grand Matoury?
x: 254 m. Mont Bourda rises to about 114 m.

q: In which year did the first rocket lift off from Kourou?
x: On 9 April 1968, with the Véronique sounding rocket.

q: On which of the Salvation Islands is landing forbidden?
x: Visitors go to Île Royale and Île Saint-Joseph. Devil's Island, where political deportees were held, is closed to landings.

q: Who has owned the Salvation Islands since 1971?
x: The French space agency (CNES); the islands also serve as a launch viewing post.

q: Which prisoner was held on Devil's Island from 1895 to 1899?
x: Captain Dreyfus, wrongly convicted, spent more than four years there.

q: What was the Dreyfus tower in Kourou?
o: A signal station linked to the Salvation Islands
x: Inaugurated in 1856, it relayed signals between the Kourou penitentiary and the islands.

q: Who were the 'Annamites' of the Montagne des Singes penal camp?
x: Political and common-law prisoners from Indochina, sent to French Guiana from 1931.

q: To whom does tradition attribute the paintings in Iracoubo church?
x: Pierre Huguet is said to have painted about 600 m² between 1891 and 1893.

q: How many convicts passed through the Transportation Camp?
x: More than 50,000. About 17,000 is the number of relégués.

q: Who did the 1885 relegation law send to French Guiana?
x: Repeat offenders, often petty criminals, interned in the colony for life.

q: Which country does the Maroni form a border with?
x: The Maroni separates French Guiana from Suriname; the Oyapock separates it from Brazil.

q: How many pirogues cross the Maroni each day, by estimates?
x: More than 1,000 crossings a day, including hundreds of children going to school.

q: Who founded Mana in 1828?
x: Mother Anne-Marie Javouhey, founder of the Sisters of Saint Joseph of Cluny.

q: By how much have leatherback turtles declined on Les Hattes beach?
x: According to Kwata. A hatchery has protected the nests since 2023.

q: How high are the Voltaire Falls?
x: About 35 m, among the highest in French Guiana.

q: In which year did the first Hmong refugees arrive in Cacao?
x: In September 1977, about 500 people.

q: Which country had the Hmong refugees of Cacao fled?
x: Laos, via Thailand, after the communist takeover.

q: How long is the Molokoï trail?
x: About 18 km between Cacao and the Coralie track, with shelters halfway.

q: Which animal of the Kaw marshes is South America's largest crocodilian?
x: Kaw shelters one of the last stable populations of black caiman.

q: How big is the Kaw-Roura marshes reserve?
x: About 94,700 ha. 2,464 ha is the Trésor reserve.

q: What colour is the male cock-of-the-rock?
x: Bright orange, with a fan-shaped crest. Females are browner.

q: Which town does the Oyapock bridge link to Saint-Georges?
x: Oiapoque, in Brazil. Albina faces Saint-Laurent, in Suriname.

q: In which year did the Oyapock bridge open to traffic?
x: Finished in 2011, it only opened on 20 March 2017.

q: What is an inselberg?
o: A rock dome rising from the forest
x: The German word means 'island mountain'. Roche Virginie is a granite dome.

q: In French Guiana, what is a pripri?
x: A freshwater marsh of the coastal plain, like the Yiyi pripris at Sinnamary.

q: How do you get to the village of Saül?
x: No road leads to Saül, in the centre of French Guiana.

q: What record does Maripasoula hold?
o: Most populous commune in French Guiana
x: About 18,360 km², slightly more than Kuwait.

q: Which university is linked to the creation of the Trésor reserve?
x: The Trésor foundation, linked to Utrecht University, bought the land.

q: What was the Vidal estate?
o: A sugar plantation worked by enslaved people
x: Established in the early 19th century, abandoned around 1880.
